searchText: <@!301186049323958275> I have updated the eth wire protocol spec with EIP-2718 Please review it: https://github.com/ethereum/devp2p/pull/177 maybe also interesting for <@!543900561460822016> because he asked for this <@194432762315407360> This doesn't align with https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2976, I'm not sure if intentional or not. According to 2976, `typed-tx = rlp(tx-type || tx-data)` should be `typed-tx = tx-type || tx-data` But we've been over this, it is not possible to include non-RLP in RLP There is no RLP list encoding here, it is just a byte array (which may later be included in an RLP list or SSZ, or whatever). The way I have documented it is the way we have implemented it in all clients `rlp([tx, tx, tx])` is fine for the higher level protocol. But individual transactions are never RLP encoded in isolation. A transaction is *just a byte array* for the networking protocol. Yes, and this is how it is documented in the spec right now The spec says that typed transactions are RLP byte arrays Since the networking protocol puts these byte arrays into lists, they end up getting RLP encoded *as a side effect of being in an RLP list*. Perhaps we are saying the same thing and I am just confused by the language used in the spec? 🤔 Yeah, we just have different understanding of the notation I will write a meta-spec for this RLP notation at some point But we mean the same thing typed transactions in RLP are byte arrays IIUC, the idea is that since `rlp([a, b, c])` (where a, b, and c are byte arrays) is identical to `rlp([rlp(a), rlp(b), rlp(c)])`, in the spec you say that the list is of RLP encoded byte arrays? I just put the `rlp(...)` because I don't want to mix the bytes concatenation `||` with the RLP notation let me check if we have precedent for this I'm OK with removing the `rlp(...)` if you want just want it to be consistent I also agree that consistency is king in this context. My mild fear (not a hill I will die on at all) is that people will think that we should be RLP encoding typed transactions elsewhere if one of the specs says "A typed transaction is `rlp(type || details)`". While we do RLP encode typed transactions in some places, that is just a side effect of the higher level datastructures they are being stored in. I get it looks like there is no precedent for this, it seems that for the last 5 years we have somehow managed to avoid specifying RLP structures where one of the byte arrays has a specific format BTW, this metalanguage consistency problem has been haunting me forever Really need to formally specify it soon I think Gavin invented this notation like `[value: P, data: B, hash: B_32]` it's not too bad, a lot of things can be described with that but it doesn't cover the case where the value is a byte array and you want to say what the internal format of it is in the other p2p specs, we use the bytes concatenation ( `||`) and some pseudo-functions like `keccak256(...)` to formally describe binary data AFAIK no commonly-agreed notation has been invented for that, people just use whatever in specs (more about this problem in https://github.com/ethereum/devp2p/issues/139) Let me know if you find other inconsistencies in the PR I'm a fan of writing specs in a common and easy to read programming language, ideally a statically typed one with a good type system. Though, even that doesn't work great when you have things that are like "a 3 byte unsigned integer". SSZ can also be used for this in some cases, it's basically a language for describing binary data with some conventions added for variable size stuff Anyway, let me know by Monday if you want something changed in the eth spec update Thanks for checking it so fast today
